neighbours.label: formal evaluation wording in legal or regulatory guidance: 'assessment/evaluation of existing …', 'analysis of whether …', 'has to be examined', 'the court may order'
fire: The bureau published interim guidance for assessment of existing pipelines under seismic loads.
The manual gives a step-by-step analysis of whether a quotation counts as fair use.
The issue of standing is something that has to be examined before the merits.
Where the breach was unintentional, the court may reduce the penalty.
The annex sets out criteria for evaluation of existing tunnels after a fire.
The course covered slope stability assessments and culvert inventory methods.
The memo offers a careful analysis of whether the exemption applies to charities.
The form collects the data necessary to evaluate each clinic's performance.
quiet: The bureau published a short history of existing pipelines in the valley.
The manual gives a list of famous quotations about fair play.
The old courthouse is something that has to be seen before you leave.
Where the path was muddy, the hikers would slow their pace.
The annex shows photographs of existing tunnels after the flood.
The course covered slope skiing and mountain photography methods.
The memo offers a warm welcome to the charities joining this year.
The form collects the names of everyone attending each clinic's picnic.

notes: Weak in probes: the best were 'analysis of whether … fair.' 0.40 and 'guidance for assessment of existing bridges' 0.31; most others 0.05-0.25. I expect this to fail on the median; the pole's real trigger is probably narrower or needs longer context than a sentence.
